issues.description: The supplied six-program workflow has missing collection indexes, lexicons, text corpora, crosswalks, WRDS/author-prepared datasets, continuation history, and Python-to-SAS imports. Frozen catalog metadata and the identifiers-only workbook do not close these inputs.

No supported producer/consumer remap among Python 1, Python 2, and Python 5 is supplied.

Python 4 contains a commented block that can create PressReleases.txt from CleanedFilings. It is a potential preparation route, not an absent algorithm; reusing it is conditional on verifying its filenames, row order, and expected list schema.
Python 5 reads MatchPRandPC.csv; none of the six supplied programs produces the index or its required article/release pair mapping.

Python 4 resumes at row 150001 and Python 5 at match 311001, appending to outputs with first-time/header blocks commented. Complete earlier chunks/header may be reused, or a supported fresh-run configuration may regenerate complete outputs when full selected input ordering and intended bounds are established. The current suffix runs alone are incomplete; neither alternative is verified, and counters/selections must not be reset blindly.

SAS uses medium and author_names to identify online/print promotions, but Python 2's active output header omits medium, author_names, and position. No compatible author producer or field mapping is supplied.

The Python programs write delimited text outputs, while SAS consumes named SAS datasets. The supplied source does not document imports or a schema-preserving conversion for PressCoverage, PressReleasesData, or AnalyzedMatches.
The supplied SAS source calls %L1, %L1_Nest, and %L1_Nest_W, whose definitions or includes are not present in this full file. Downstream L1_0 and L1_i tables therefore have unresolved producers.
SAS downloads gc15 to mydir.wrds_gc15_20170912 but the next step reads mydir.wrds_gc15_20170621. The earlier checkpoint's provenance and intended date are unknown.
The Excel PROC IMPORT is inside a SAS block comment, but the following PressCoverage2020 consumer and Table 8 analysis are active. Python 2 produces a differently named text file and no import step.

The SEC page requires a declared User-Agent; the supplied urllib request uses urlopen without request headers. A compliant identifier and request pacing need configuration before any separately authorized collection.

The collection scripts include SMTP notification calls. Notification is operational and not a research input; disable it in a working-copy configuration before any future collection. No email, contact, or network action was performed.

evidence.quote:
1CollectMediaCoverage.py: Python script used to collect the text of WSJ articles from Factiva

2AnalyzeMediaCoverage.py: Python script used to clean article text and calculate linguistic variables used in the study (e.g., percentage of negative words and sentences with quotes)

3CollectPressReleases.py: Python script used to collect the text of firms' earnings press releases from SEC EDGAR

4AnalyzePressReleases.py: Python script used to clean press release text and calculate complexity variables used in the study (e.g., readability and specificity)

5CompareMediaCoverageAndPressReleases.py: Python script used to compare earnings press releases and the associated WSJ articles via the Jaccard (1901) similarity measure

Guest_MediaEarnings_FinalDatasetAndAnalyses.sas: SAS program used to combine the raw outputs from the above mentioned Python programs with other financial and accounting data (e.g., Compustat and CRSP).
That is, this code converts raw data into the final dataset used in the study. This file also includes code that produces the key tables and figures in the paper.
